STEP 1 - Scene: This is a simple plate of cooked meats: braised or roasted chicken pieces, a stewed lamb or goat shank-type piece, and a whole red apple.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The white ridged plate looks like a side or small dinner plate, about 22 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 11² ≈ 380 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roasted/braised chicken pieces (upper left; wings and back, bony)
- Chicken feet or wing tips with dark glaze (bottom)
- Braised lamb/goat shank (center)
- A small whole apple

STEP 4 - Area:

| Item | Share of plate | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken pieces | 14% | 53 cm² |
| Glazed chicken bits | 7% | 27 cm² |
| Shank | 12% | 46 cm² |
| Apple | 8% | 30 cm² |
| **Total covered** | **~41%** | (plausible, as the plate is about half empty) |

STEP 5 - Volume:

| Item | Calculation | Gross volume |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken pieces | 53 cm² × 3 cm | 159 ml |
| Glazed bits | 27 cm² × 2 cm | 54 ml |
| Shank | 46 cm² × 3.5 cm | 161 ml |
| Apple | small, ~6.5 cm diameter sphere | ~140 ml |

STEP 6 - Grams: The chicken and shank are bony and irregular, so I used a density of about 0.7 rather than 1.0.

| Item | Calculation | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken pieces | 159 ml × 0.7 | ~110 g (edible portion less) |
| Glazed bits | 54 ml × 0.7 | ~38 g |
| Shank | 161 ml × 0.8 | ~130 g |
| Apple | 140 ml × 0.8 | ~115 g |

STEP 7 - Energy: The calorie figures are per 100 g as plated, including bone.

| Item | Calculation | Energy |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken pieces | 110 g × 200 | 220 kcal |
| Glazed bits | 38 g × 180 | 68 kcal |
| Shank | 130 g × 190 | 247 kcal |
| Apple | 115 g × 52 | 60 kcal |

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 393 g and 595 kcal. That is plausible for a half-covered plate of bony meats plus an apple.
